cards.text: In those days, there was no king in Israel. A Levite living way out in the remote hill country of Ephraim takes a concubine from Bethlehem in Judah. Friend, I'll be straight with you: this is one of the hardest stories in the whole Bible, so stay close to me on this one.

cards.question: The Levite's concubine is unfaithful to him and leaves him. Where does she go?

answers.text: Her father's house in Bethlehem
The house of the LORD in Shiloh
Her sister's house in Hebron

cards.text: She's been there four months. Then her husband gets up and goes after her, taking his servant and a pair of donkeys.

cards.question: The Levite travels all the way to Bethlehem after his concubine. What does he go there to do?

answers.text: Speak kindly to her and bring her back
Demand payment from her father
Bring her before the town elders

cards.question: The girl brings the Levite into her father's house. True or false: her father is unhappy to see him.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: He gladly welcomes him and persuades him to stay. So the Levite stays three days, eating, drinking and lodging there.

cards.question: On the fourth day, the Levite is up early and ready to leave. What does the girl's father tell him first?

answers.text: Have a bite of bread before you go
The roads are too dangerous today
My daughter is not ready to leave

cards.text: So the two of them sit down and eat and drink together. Then the father asks him to stay the night, and when the man gets up to go, his father-in-law talks him into it.

cards.question: On the fifth day, the Levite gets up early to leave. True or false: he's on the road by morning.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: They wait until late afternoon and eat again, and then the father says the day's almost over, so please spend the night. Friend, this man is getting SNOOZED by his father-in-law. Every time he stands up, BOOP, five more minutes.

cards.question: The father-in-law begs the Levite to spend the night one more time. What does the Levite do?

answers.text: Leaves anyway with his concubine
Asks to stay a whole week
Sends his servant home alone

cards.text: He finally IGNORES the snooze button, and off they go with the two saddled donkeys. They come near Jebus, that's Jerusalem, and the day is almost gone.

cards.question: It's getting dark near Jebus. What does the Levite's servant suggest?

answers.text: Stop and spend the night in Jebus
Turn back to the house in Bethlehem
Keep walking all through the night

cards.question: The Levite says no to stopping in Jebus. Why?

answers.text: It is a city of foreigners with no Israelites
Its gates are already shut for the night
He has made enemies who live there

cards.question: The Levite wants to push on to an Israelite town. He says they'll try to spend the night in Gibeah or ___.

answers.text: Ramah
Hebron
Jericho

cards.text: The sun sets as they get near Gibeah in Benjamin, so they turn in to lodge there. The Levite goes in and sits down in the city square.

cards.question: The Levite and his group are sitting in Gibeah's city square at nightfall. True or false: someone quickly takes them into his home.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: That evening, an old man comes in from his work in the field. He's from the hill country of Ephraim too, living here in Gibeah, where the men are Benjamites.

cards.question: The old man looks up and sees the traveler in the city square. What does he ask him?

answers.text: Where he is going and where he came from
Whether he can pay for a room tonight
Why he brought his donkeys into town

cards.text: The Levite tells him they're traveling from Bethlehem in Judah, headed home to the hill country of Ephraim. He says he's going to the house of the LORD, but no one has taken him into his home.

cards.question: No one in Gibeah has taken the Levite in. What does he tell the old man about their supplies?

answers.text: They already have everything they need
They have run out of bread and wine
Their donkeys have not eaten all day

cards.question: The old man says, "Peace to you," and offers to supply everything the Levite needs. What's the one thing he tells him not to do?

answers.text: Spend the night in the square
Tell anyone where he is from
Leave the house before morning

cards.text: So he brings them home and feeds the donkeys, and they wash their feet and eat and drink. Finally, friend, a door opens.
But while they're enjoying themselves, the wicked men of the city suddenly surround the house. They start pounding on the door.

cards.question: The wicked men of Gibeah are pounding on the old man's door. Who do they demand he bring out?

answers.text: The man who came to his house
The old man himself
The Levite's servant

cards.text: The old man goes out and says, "No, my brothers, do not do this wicked thing!" He reminds them this man is a guest in his house.

cards.question: True or false: the old man offers to bring out his own virgin daughter and the Levite's concubine instead.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: But the men won't listen to him. So the Levite takes his concubine and sends her outside to them, and they rape her and abuse her throughout the night.

cards.question: At dawn, the men let the concubine go. Where does she go?

answers.text: Back to the house where her master is staying
Back to her father's house in Bethlehem
Out to the gate of the city

cards.text: She collapses at the doorway and lies there until it's light. In the morning, her master opens the doors to go on his journey, and there she is, with her hands on the threshold.

cards.question: The Levite finds his concubine collapsed in the doorway. What does he say to her?

answers.text: Get up and let us go
Forgive me for what I did
Wait here while I find help

cards.text: But there's no response, so he puts her on his donkey and sets out for home. When he gets there, he takes a knife and cuts her limb by limb into twelve pieces.

cards.question: Where does the Levite send the twelve pieces?

answers.text: Throughout the territory of Israel
To the elders of Gibeah
To her father in Bethlehem

cards.question: Everyone who sees it says nothing like this has been seen or done since when?

answers.text: The day Israel came out of Egypt
The days of the great flood
The day Joshua crossed the Jordan

cards.question: The people who see it don't stay silent. What do they call on Israel to do?

answers.text: Think it over and speak up
Stay quiet and move on
Forget it ever happened

cards.text: And that's where we'll pause, friend, with all of Israel staring at something no one has ever seen. Trust me, this story is far from finished.

findings.problem: The card tells that the father gladly welcomes the Levite, which is Judges 19:3, but it cites only Judges 19:4. The citation should be Judges 19:3-4.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the waiting and the father's plea, the SNOOZED line, and the BOOP line. Story cards after the opening card are 1 to 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the second town name the Levite says (Ramah). Nothing on the earlier cards lets the baker reason this out, so it tests wording they haven't seen, not meaning. Ramah also doesn't move the story forward, because they stop at Gibeah.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "The old man himself" doesn't make sense. The men are shouting at the old man and telling him to bring someone out, so asking him to bring out himself is not believable.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: This story card carries three beats: the men won't listen, the Levite sends his concubine outside, and the men abuse her through the night. It should be split.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: The question says "Everyone who sees it." The word "it" points back to the twelve pieces on an earlier card, which the baker can no longer see.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The setup line "don't stay silent" gives away the right answer ("speak up"). It also rules out both wrong answers, "Stay quiet and move on" and "Forget it ever happened."

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The question says the people "call on Israel." Judges 19:30 doesn't say who "Think it over, take counsel, and speak up!" is spoken to, so the card shouldn't name a listener. The question also says "who see it" without saying what "it" is.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The card says "all of Israel staring at something no one has ever seen." Judges 19:30 says only "everyone who saw it," and it compares this to everything since the day Israel came out of Egypt, not to all of history. "All of Israel" and "ever" both stretch the text, and this line is not a joke.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: This passage contains attempted sexual assault, rape and the cutting up of a woman's body. The docs say the app is for adults, kids can still play, and Papa Dorin is always clean, but they don't say how to handle violence like this. Card 7 and card 8 leave out what the men demand in Judges 19:22 ("so we can have relations with him"), which makes the old man's words about a "wicked thing" and "outrage" harder to follow. Card 11 states the rape plainly. Several choice cards earn sugar cookies for answers about these events: card 10 (the old man offers his daughter and the concubine), card 12 (where the concubine goes after the abuse), card 14 (what the Levite says to her) and card 16 (where the pieces are sent).
findings.question: For passages with sexual violence and graphic violence, how directly should Papa Dorin tell what happens, including the men's demand in Judges 19:22? Should the abuse and the dismemberment be the subject of choice cards that earn cookies, or only be told on story cards?
